states.name: Alabama
states.min_age: Under 16 may not work except in agricultural service, but 14 and 15 year olds may work outside school hours and during school vacation periods, in jobs the law allows (Alabama Code 25-8-33, from the state statute PDF).
states.permit: The employer, not the teen, must get a Class I Child Labor Certificate from the Alabama Department of Labor for each location that employs 14 and 15 year olds ($15 per location), and a Class II certificate for 16 and 17 year olds. The statute also says 14 and 15 year olds need an Eligibility to Work Form, which the school issues (Alabama Code 25-8-45 and 25-8-46, from the statute PDF).
states.hours: Ages 14 and 15, while school is in session: no more than 3 hours on a school day, 8 hours on a non-school day and 18 hours a week. Work only between 7 am and 7 pm, and no more than 6 days a week. In summer vacation: no more than 8 hours a day or 40 a week, only between 7 am and 9 pm. This comes from Alabama Code 25-8-36, in the state statute PDF.
states.who_to_ask: Alabama Department of Labor, Child Labor Office (the page lists the child labor enforcement inspector, J. Adam Strickland).
states.page_title: Child Labor - Alabama Department of Labor (hours, minimum age and Eligibility to Work Form also read in the state's PDF https://www.labor.alabama.gov/docs/law/UC_ChildLabor_ChildLaborStatutes2012.pdf, a 2012 statute compilation; the HTML page does not list hours, minimum age or the Eligibility to Work Form)

states.hours: For 14 and 15 year olds, the page lists Nebraska limits and federal limits side by side. Nebraska limits: no more than 8 hours in one day and 48 hours in one week, and not before 6 a.m. or after 10 p.m. The page does not say whether the 8 and 48 hour limits are for school weeks or non-school weeks. Federal limits: no more than 3 hours on a school day and 18 hours in a school week, and no more than 8 hours on a non-school day and 40 hours in a non-school week. Federal limits also say not before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m. (9 p.m. from June 1 to Labor Day). The page says employers must follow whichever law is more restrictive. states.who_to_ask: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI), Wage and Hour Division.

states.quote: Minors age 14-17 are not issued individual work permits in Oregon.
states.source_excerpt: Minors age 14-17 are not issued individual work permits in Oregon. Click here for summaries of youth employment laws including industry-specific resources.

states.hours: For 14 and 15 year olds: work only between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m., or until 9 p.m. during school vacations. The page we read does not give daily or weekly hour limits.

states.quote: No child under fourteen (14) years of age shall be employed
states.source_excerpt: No child under fourteen (14) years of age shall be employed or permitted or suffered to work at any time in any business or industrial establishment in this state.

states.name: South Carolina
states.min_age: A minor can begin work at age 14, with limits on the type of work and hours.
states.permit: No. South Carolina does not issue work permits for minors. The minor gives the employer a copy of a birth certificate or driver's license that shows birth date.
states.hours: For 14 and 15 year olds, when school is in session: up to 3 hours a day and 18 hours a week, only from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. When school is out: up to 8 hours a day and 40 hours a week, until 9 p.m. in summer.
states.who_to_ask: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation, Office of Wages and Child Labor.
states.page_title: SCLLR
states.quote: A minor can begin work at age 14.
states.source_excerpt: A minor can begin work at age 14. However, the child labor laws have restrictions on what type of work can be performed and limitations on hours of work.

states.name: South Dakota
states.min_age: Not stated on the page we read.
states.permit: Not stated on the page we read.
states.hours: For children under 16: no more than 4 hours on a school day and 20 hours in a school week. No more than 8 hours on a non-school day and 40 hours in a non-school week. No work after 10 p.m. on a school night. Where federal law is stricter, federal law applies.
states.who_to_ask: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation, for youth employment questions and complaints.
states.page_title: Employment Laws - Youth Employment
states.quote: Children younger than 16 years may not be employed
states.source_excerpt: Children younger than 16 years may not be employed: In any occupation dangerous to life, health or morals * For more than four hours per school day or 20 hours per school week * For more than eight hours per non-school day or 40 hours per non-school week * Later than 10 p.m.

states.name: Tennessee

states.name: Utah
states.min_age: Not stated on the page we read.
states.permit: Minors are not required to have a work permit for employment purposes. School districts are expected to help employers confirm a minor's age with an age certificate.
states.hours: Ages 16 and 17: no limit on hours. Under 16: not during school hours (except as authorized), not more than 4 hours before and after school hours, not more than 8 hours in 24 hours, and not more than 40 hours in a week. No work before 5 am or after 9:30 pm unless the next day is not a school day.
states.who_to_ask: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division.
states.page_title: Wage Claim - Utah Labor Commission
states.quote: Minors are not required to have a work permit for employment purposes.
states.source_excerpt: Work Permits For Minors: Minors are not required to have a work permit for employment purposes. However, all school districts are expected to cooperate with employers' requests for information regarding a prospective minor employee's age (i.e., age certificate.)

states.name: Vermont
states.min_age: Children under 14 generally may not do non-agricultural work. Exceptions include work for a parent or custodian, actors and performers, and newspaper carriers.
states.permit: An employment certificate is not required unless the minor is under 16 and works during school hours outside an approved school or job training course. The booklet does not say who issues it.
states.hours: For 14 and 15 year olds: no work during school hours, or before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m. (after 9 p.m. between June 1 and Labor Day). Limits are 3 hours on a school day, 8 hours on a non-school day, 18 hours in a school week, and 40 hours in a non-school week. No work on more than 6 days in a week.
states.who_to_ask: Ask the Vermont Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Program.
states.page_title: Important Information for Employers of Minors in the State of Vermont on Federal and State Child Labor Laws (WH-30)
states.quote: Children under 14 years of age are generally prohibited
states.source_excerpt: • Children under 14 years of age are generally prohibited from performing any non-agricultural work.

states.name: West Virginia
states.min_age: Fourteen is the minimum age that a minor may be legally employed, with exceptions such as a business solely owned by a parent or guardian.
states.permit: Yes for ages 14 and 15: an age certificate is required before any job. It needs a job promise, parental consent, proof of school attendance, and proof of age. For ages 16 and 17 it is generally not required by law, though an employer may ask for one. The WV Division of Labor Commissioner or an authorized representative issues all age certificates.
states.hours: For 14 and 15 year olds: no work before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m. on school days, or after 9 p.m. in summer when school is not in session (Memorial Day through Labor Day). No more than 3 hours on a school day and 18 hours in a school week. No more than 8 hours on a non-school day and 40 hours in a non-school week. No work during school hours.
states.who_to_ask: Ask the West Virginia Division of Labor, Wage and Hour section.
states.phone: Not stated on the page we read.
states.page_title: Child Labor FAQ | WV Division of Labor
states.quote: Fourteen is the minimum age that a minor may be legally employed
states.source_excerpt: What is the minimum age that a child may go to work? Fourteen is the minimum age that a minor may be legally employed unless that minor is working for a business solely owned by a parent or guardian, or the type of work being performed is not covered by state child labor laws.

states.name: Wyoming
states.min_age: Not stated on the page we read. The page is written for ages 14 to 17.
states.permit: You do not need a work permit to start a job in Wyoming. Your employer needs proof of your age on file, such as a birth certificate or another ID.
states.hours: Ages 14 and 15: not during school hours, no more than 3 hours on a school day and 18 hours in a school week. Only between 7 am and 7 pm (9 pm from June 1 to Labor Day). Parents cannot override these limits.
states.who_to_ask: Wyoming Department of Workforce Services, Labor Standards Division (Cheyenne and Casper offices).
states.phone: Not stated on the page we read.
states.page_title: Frequently Asked Questions (Wyoming Labor Standards)
states.quote: Wyoming does not require minors to obtain work permits.
states.source_excerpt: Q: Do I need a work permit to work as a minor? A: No. Wyoming does not require minors to obtain work permits. Your employer just needs proof of your age on file, such as a birth certificate or another form of identification.
